title: The six operations: ambient typing
statement:
Use the global finite-field and coefficient datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p_0$, $\ell\ne p_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. At finite level give $A$ the discrete topology, use left modules, and use the small sites in the common larger universe fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The finite-level ambient notation is $D(T,A)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and its bounded-below subcategory $D^+(T,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The small category $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ is the bounded constructible finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with derived-complete integral, rationalized, and common-stage coefficients as specified there. All schemes in the following are finite type over $k$; at the higher coefficient stages use the operations specified by the cited definitions and their finite-level realizations.

For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] the six operations are the following
functors of ambient categories:

1. **(i)** the derived pullback, the derived tensor product and the derived
internal Hom
$$
\begin{aligned}
Lf^*&:D(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(X,\Lambda),\\
-\otimes^L_\Lambda-&:D(Y,\Lambda)\times D(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Lambda),\\
\RHom_\Lambda(-,-)&:D(Y,\Lambda)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Lambda),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $\RHom_\Lambda$ is the internal Hom: for each $K$, the functor $K\otimes^L_\Lambda-$ is left adjoint to $\RHom_\Lambda(K,-)$, naturally in $K$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom];
1. **(ii)** the derived direct image
$Rf_*:D^+(X,\Lambda)\to D^+(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image];
1. **(iii)** extension by zero $j_!:D^+(U,\Lambda)\to D^+(X,\Lambda)$ for an
open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact];
1. **(iv)** the compact-support direct image $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$ attached to a
compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, as a functor of
ambient categories, independent of the compactification on the bounded-below étale-origin
complexes [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, prop-compactification-coherence-detailed];
1. **(v)** *the ambient exceptional right adjoint* $Rf^{\times}$, an
*optional and conditional* notion: it is not defined, it is *assumed*: a
functor of ambient categories
$$
Rf^{\times}:D(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(X,\Lambda)
$$
which is right adjoint to $Rf_!$ of (iv). Its *existence* — together
with $\operatorname{FullCD}$ for the proper part of the compactification and
the compatibility of units and counits with refinements — is the *ambient
exceptional right adjoint datum* of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint];
1. **(vi)** *the exceptional inverse image* $Rf^!$, a functor of the
small categories
$$
Rf^!:\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dctf(X,\Lambda),
$$
*defined unconditionally* for every separated finite-type morphism
$f:X\to Y$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, as follows. At a finite stage
$\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ let $f^{\times}:D(Y_{\Et},A)\to D(X_{\Et},A)$ be a chosen
right adjoint of the étale compact-support functor
$Rf^{\Et}_!:D(X_{\Et},A)\to D(Y_{\Et},A)$ on the unbounded derived categories
of the small étale sites, which exists by Brown representability ([def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]). Every
object of $\Dctf(Y,A)$ is of étale origin,
$L\cong\nu_Y^*G$ with $G\in\Dctf(Y_{\Et},A)$ unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen identification $\nu_Y^*G\cong L$
([lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]; Stacks Tag 09AK, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-constructible), and one *defines*
$$
Rf^!L:=\nu_X^*\,f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}L\;\cong\;\nu_X^*\,f^{\times}G ,
$$
the étale right adjoint transported along the étale/pro-étale
comparison. The defining composite makes sense on all of $D^+(Y_{\Proet},A)$. For the displayed natural isomorphism, apply [sk-prop-sf-comparison] with scheme $Y$, ring $A$ and $K=G$: bounded constructibility implies $G\in D^+(Y_{\Et},A)$, so the unit $G\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{Y,*}\nu_Y^*G$ is invertible. Composing this unit with $R\nu_{Y,*}$ of the chosen identification $\nu_Y^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ identifies $G$ with $R\nu_{Y,*}L$; applying $\nu_X^*f^{\times}$ gives the displayed natural isomorphism. The same cited comparison gives full faithfulness on $D^+$, so the uniqueness assertion above is relative to the chosen identification. Its two
defining properties are *theorems*, not hypotheses: the *adjunction*
$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Rf^!L)$,
natural in every bounded-below $K$ of étale origin — in particular every
$K\in\Dctf(X,A)$ — and every bounded-below $L$, with units and counits
compatible with refinements of the compactification
([thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]); and the *preservation*
$Rf^!\Dctf(Y,A)\subseteq\Dctf(X,A)$, with explicit bounds on the
constructible interval and on the Tor amplitude
([def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (v), on its separated-scheme domain). At the
adic stages $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$ the functor is defined levelwise on
the normalized systems, $Rf^!(L_n)_n=(Rf^!_nL_n)_n$, the finite-reduction
isomorphisms $Rf^!_n(L_n)\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}\cong Rf^!_m(L_m)$
($1\le m\le n$) in the coherent-system construction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (also [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (vii) on its stated domain) making the result a normalized
system again, followed by rationalization and the common-stage construction.

At finite coefficients, when the ambient functor $Rf^{\times}$ of (v) exists and satisfies the
preservation clauses (2) and (3) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], its restriction to $\Dctf$
agrees naturally with $Rf^!$: both represent $K\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!K,L)$ on the full bounded constructible category, and clause (3) restricts their Yoneda identification to $\Dctf$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At the integral, rational and common-stage coefficients this comparison uses the compatible finite adjoint families, quotient and scalar comparisons, and uniform bounds required by [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]; the finite identifications pass through the specified coefficient constructions.

*Warning.* The existence hypothesis of the ambient datum of (v),
$\operatorname{FullCD}$ on *every* pro-étale sheaf of $A$-modules, *fails*
already for the structure morphism of an elliptic curve $E$ over
$\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$, where $p$ and $r$ are distinct primes: there is a pro-étale
$A$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $E$ with $H^n(E_{\Proet},\mathcal F)\neq0$
for every $n\ge1$, and for that morphism $Rf_!=Rf_*$ does not preserve the
coproduct $\bigoplus_n\mathcal F[n]$ and has no right adjoint on
$D(E_{\Proet},A)$, nor on $D^+$ (the explanatory warning of [sk-def-sf-admissible], already recorded among this node's blueprint forward references). This warning is a forward explanation of the optional datum, not a prerequisite for defining any of the functors above.

split_report.summary: Split the bundled definition by its existing operation and coefficient definitions, including exact extension by zero, constructible origin and Tor comparison. Repaired the earlier attempt: removed its added unit metadata; removed its incorrect citation of the FullCD definition for a counterexample; distinguished ambient preservation assumptions from constructible preservation; made the coefficient context and witness-relative uniqueness explicit. The existing sk-def-sf-admissible already states the full warning, so retain that as an explanatory forward reference, as recorded by the inherited blueprint_forward_refs, rather than a defining dependency. No new node is needed. The current generic derived tensor/internal-Hom definition explicitly supplies the parameterized adjunction, which the older construction-only definition does not state. Second reading: parameterized the tensor-Hom adjunction, made the exceptional composite the defining functor and the lift formula an isomorphism, unified the proper-map notation, and distinguished finite conditional agreement from its coherent higher coefficient passage. Made the counterexample's distinct-prime hypotheses explicit from its source remark. Landing-return repair: reread the current bounded-below sk-prop-sf-comparison statement and made its exact use explicit in clause (vi): specialize its unit to (Y,A,G), use boundedness of G, then compose with the chosen lift identification. Constructible origin and Tor preservation remain separate citations; the comparison is not being cited for those stronger statements. Repackaging with the required delivery tool rebases this retained split onto current origin/newtargets-dag. Compared returned head d78a4208b5988db7c1acb2ae2e72879fe8d29805 directly with fetched origin fcb3647c5d6ead53563c2cb028c1057347440911 by read-only Git-object decoding. Only the comparison statement changed among the 21 dependencies: it now spells out discrete coefficients, left modules, common-universe and derived-category conventions, and the small cofiltered presentation for the unused affine clause. Made the applicable finite-level coefficient and universe conventions explicit and checked the unchanged unit/full-faithfulness conclusions under them. Independent second reading: explicitly restricted compactification independence in clause (iv) to bounded-below etale-origin complexes, matching the declared domain of def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed; reran the Mathlib search and the read-only current-origin dependency comparison.
split_report.blueprint: Clauses (i)-(iii) use the existing derived-operation definitions; clause (iv) uses compact-support and coherence; clause (v) uses the optional ambient datum; clause (vi) uses the coherent finite/integral exceptional construction and comparison, with stability on its stated domain. The final explanatory warning refers forward to the already existing sk-def-sf-admissible; it supplies no data used in these constructions.
